questions.q: What is an incremental (delta) load, and why does it matter at scale?
options: Loading only the rows that are new or changed since the last run, instead of reloading the entire source every time
Loading the source table in small random batches for no particular reason
A load that only ever runs once and is never scheduled again
A load that skips the destination table entirely and writes only to a log file
questions.explain: A full load re-pulls every row every run, which stops scaling once a source table gets large — an incremental load pulls only what actually changed.

questions.q: What is a watermark in the context of an incremental load?
options: A saved value, usually the maximum modified-date or key processed last run, used to know where to resume extracting from
A visual overlay printed on report PDFs
A password required to open the SSIS package
The name of the destination table
questions.explain: The watermark is how the package remembers 'how far it got' last time, so the next run can extract only rows newer than that value.

questions.q: Which two Chapter 4 transformations combine to route new rows to an insert and existing rows to an update in an incremental load pattern?
options: Lookup and Conditional Split
Sort and Aggregate
Merge Join and Data Conversion
Derived Column and Union All
questions.explain: Lookup checks each extracted row against the destination's business key, and Conditional Split routes matched rows to an update path and unmatched rows to an insert path.

questions.q: Where in the pattern does an Execute SQL Task typically appear, and why?
options: Before the data flow, to read the saved watermark, and after it, to save the new watermark
Only at the very end, to email a completion notice
It never appears in an incremental load pattern
Only inside the Lookup transformation's configuration
questions.explain: Execute SQL Task reads last run's watermark before extraction starts and writes the new maximum value back once the load finishes.

questions.q: How does a general incremental load pattern differ from the Slowly Changing Dimension Transformation covered next lesson?
options: The pattern is a general-purpose incremental extract strategy for any table, while the SCD Transformation is a specialized component built specifically for dimension tables with Type 1/Type 2 change tracking
They are the exact same feature under two different names
The SCD Transformation replaces the need for any watermark or extract logic entirely
Incremental loads only work with flat files, never SQL Server tables
questions.explain: Incremental extraction and the SCD Transformation solve overlapping but distinct problems — extraction is about pulling only changed source rows, while the SCD Transformation is about correctly applying those changes to a dimension table.
